messages:
alex: Heads-up — after landing PR 4f2a9c2 yesterday we saw a 12-18% p95 latency regression on our 8k seq perf job. I ran a quick nsys capture, attaching timeline link: https://perf.internal/reports/4f2a9c2-nsys
maya: Ugh. Which part regressed? kernel selection or batching?
olivia: I saw an increase in memcpy time and a bunch of small kernels firing instead of the fused attention kernel on A100. nvprof sample below.
```
== PROFILES ==
Kernel: matmul_fused_attn  avg_ms=0.45  calls=120
Kernel: attention_split_kernel  avg_ms=0.12 calls=980
mempcy H2D avg_ms=0.03 calls=1600
KV_cache_lookup avg_ms=0.02 calls=2400
```
julian: That looks like kernel selector picked non-fused path due to shape/stride mismatch. Did the PR change the alignment heuristics?
sre-bot: Deploy 2025-10-12T09:12:03 completed for canary pool.
alex: PR changed the kernel fallback thresholds and added a conservative path for odd sequence chunking (commit 4f2a9c2). The intention was to avoid OOM on weird model shapes.
maya: Can you run a before/after perfetto trace comparison? perfetto links make hotspots obvious.
alex: Uploaded two traces: before (commit 3e7b1a8) https://perf.internal/traces/3e7b1a8-perfetto and after (4f2a9c2) https://perf.internal/traces/4f2a9c2-perfetto. Key observation: after = more small attention kernels + double memcpy during KV refill.
olivia: I bisected locally: `git bisect` pointed to 4f2a9c2 -> the patch that changed kernel_selection.cpp: line 182 threshold from 256->512 and added an extra memcpy for cache alignment.
julian: Can you paste the kernel selector snippet?
alex: Sure:
```
// kernel_selection.cpp (trimmed)
if (seq_len % 16 != 0 || head_dim % 8 != 0) {
  // fall back to safe split attention to avoid misaligned loads
  use_split_attn = true;
  // pad KV to 64-byte boundary (extra memcpy)
  pad_kv = true;
} else if (seq_len <= 512 && head_dim == 64) {
  use_fused_attn = true;
}
```
maya: The pad_kv=true is the smoking gun — extra memcpy + cache thrash. For our workloads padding is unnecessary; GPUs can handle unaligned loads with lower perf penalty than extra kernels.
alex: Agreed. Quick experiment: revert pad_kv default and only enable for batches > 64k tokens. Ran a canary with that change: p95 dropped back ~14% and nvprof shows fused kernel back. New trace: https://perf.internal/traces/4f2a9c2-revert-pad.
olivia: We should add a microbenchmark for seq_len/head_dim combos to prevent regression. Also update kernel selector tests and add a perf regression alert to CI when fused kernel disappears for canonical shapes.
julian: Proposed remediation: revert pad_kv change + add opt-in flag for strict alignment; add unit/integration perf test that records kernel counts (fused vs split) using nsys on a synthetic harness.
alex: I'll open PR with revert + tests. Preliminary title: "revert: avoid unnecessary KV padding; add kernel-selection perf tests". Assigning to me and @maya for review.
maya: Thanks — also file an incident note so oncall knows the regression cause and fix timeline.
sre-bot: Incident created: INC-20251012-7 (perf regression due to kernel selector change).
alex: One more: we should add a small flamegraph snapshot to the changelog entry so reviewers can spot perf regressions quickly.
olivia: Agreed. I'll push a perf-test harness to eng-runtime/perf with config matrix for head_dim in {32,64,128} and seq_len in {128,512,2048}.
julian: OK. After PR lands let's run a full dedicated pool smoke test and then promote to canary.
alex: Will do. Thanks all :thumbsup:
